study_design: Case-control study of newly diagnosed prostate cancer cases and noncancerous controls.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Between 2005 and 2006, this prospective case-control study was performed on patients referred to Sina and Imam University hospitals, Tehran, Iran; it included 62 men with clinicopathologically confirmed diagnosis of prostate cancer (case group) and 68 men with no detectable prostate cancer [normal digital rectal examination and prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level] or any other malignant disease (control group).
reason: The case-control study evaluates newly diagnosed prostate cancer generally. No advanced, high-grade, metastatic, lethal, or other aggressive endpoint is analyzed. The total sample is left null because the abstract reports separate group counts rather than an explicit total, and totals are not inferred from case and control counts.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Serum selenium was inversely associated with prostate cancer risk. After adjustment for age, body mass index (BMI), and smoking, the odds ratio was 0.16 and 95% confidence intervals were 0.06 to 0.47 (P trendq = 0.001) comparing the highest with the lowest tertile (> or = 89.3 microg/l).
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate is for prostate cancer risk overall, with no aggressive disease definition or stratification.
